title: The Redemption Margin Kept Standing Above What a Receipt Covers
content:
A margin is kept standing above what the receipt still covers, because a receipt has to be redeemable in grain of the grade it names. This rule governs warehouse receipts issued against Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements.

## Clause

Where the receipt covers the large-receipt count of 25000 bushels or more and a quality recheck has been asked for on the agreement, the wide redemption margin of 1250 bushels is kept.

Where the receipt covers the large-receipt count or more, or a quality recheck has been asked for on the agreement, the standard margin of 400 bushels is kept.

And otherwise no redemption margin is kept.

## Judgement table

| Bushels the receipt covers | A quality recheck has been asked for on the agreement | Margin kept |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 25000 or more | yes | 1250 |
| 25000 or more | no | 400 |
| under 25000 | yes | 400 |
| under 25000 | no | none |

The count is read as at or above: a receipt covering exactly 25000 bushels reaches the large-receipt count, and one covering 24999 does not.

What is counted on the second particular is whether any request for a quality recheck stands on the agreement at all, not how many.

## Worked margins, on hypothetical figures

**A receipt covering 31000 bushels on an agreement carrying a request for a quality recheck.** Both limbs stand, so 1250 bushels are kept.

**A receipt covering 31000 bushels with no recheck asked for.** One limb stands, so 400 bushels are kept.

**A receipt covering 9000 bushels on an agreement carrying a request for a quality recheck.** One limb stands, so 400 bushels are kept.

**A receipt covering 9000 bushels with no recheck asked for.** Neither limb stands, so no redemption margin is kept.
